design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (credit_card_promotions, env_0062), round 4. Draw: prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[4,5]; statement minimum 4, courtesy credit 5.
ROUND-4 CHANGES (source misses found by the renderer and KB audit; no scored value moved): the rules now state the assembly once and generically (the share, the part credited outright, the credit basis; the core and the parts added or taken off), with each factor saying how it enters; the printed-minimum clause is carried in full in the overwrite for every use outside the desk payment; the below-floor tier states that payments since closing still come off; past due is never below zero; a reversal of a fee posted after the closing takes nothing off; scope lines moved into the factor sentences they concern; rounding uses integer half-up and integer-cent ceilings, with no tolerance constants; tool docstrings state only the ledger entry written.
ROUND-3 CHANGES: dispute_exclusion now leaves out the share of any open disputed charge carried in the statement's balance, whatever cycle it posted in (Reg Z 1026.13(d)(1); R2-F2, R2-F5); reversal_refigure is labelled parameter, like dispute_exclusion, since both put an amount into the deductions (R2-O4); the minimum rule states its scope (at most one fee reversal since the closing and at most one open dispute) instead of a most-recent read (R2-O5); the courtesy allowance shared with returned payment fees is taken in posting order (R2-O1); the persona's dispute line matches the single 214.60 ledger row.
ROUND-2 CHANGES: courtesy credit restructured for factor independence (repeat_fee_basis now decides only the share base and the outright part; the combined share and the credit are plain bindings); rounding is half up in compute exactly as the rules say (int(x*100+0.5)/100, no float round). Statement minimum rebuilt: fee_component (one netting rule, F-4) and installment_rate (base table under another name, F-6) removed; the plan rate is now a plain read of the base equal_pay_apr_pct; new factors dispute_exclusion (Reg Z 1026.13 billing-error dispute left out of the minimum) and reversal_refigure (parameter: how a fee reversal posted since the statement re-figures the minimum). World: an outside purchase of 214.60 on 2026-09-08 under an open billing-error dispute submitted 2026-10-02 (within 60 days of the statement); the September statement is re-simulated with it (printed minimum 158.51). Both courtesy overwrites now name the sibling returned-payment courtesy schedule in their tails.
SCOPE: task 0 = card_ext_courtesy_fee_credit (card_fee_reversal on a late fee, agent) -> card_ext_statement_minimum_payment (card_payment, user). Task 1 holds the returned-fee courtesy, the deferred interest assessment and the cardholder's payment direction.
WHY A GOOD TEST: the caller asks only to pay this month's minimum. The minimum rule waits on the courtesy credit owed on the September-cycle late fee (state form); the printed 158.51 is stale twice over (the courtesy credit and an open billing-error dispute). The agent must work the courtesy matrix (five factors, one cross-product) and then re-figure the minimum (four factors).
PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root minimum (owner user) <- courtesy (value_input, gate rev_off, state form). Sentence: "The minimum payment the desk takes on a statement is not fixed until every late fee posted in that statement's cycle that meets the courtesy credit conditions carries its courtesy credit." Only the late-fee courtesy schedule writes courtesy reversals on late fees. Unresolved at opening: no reversal cites fee 2026-09-19. Skip run: 152.07 instead of 116.02.
FACTOR CARD courtesy (35.00; all-baseline 41.00): history_share 0.50 -> base 41.00; service_plan_bonus 0.15 (hazard + alignment on the card) -> 30.50; card_spend_bonus 0.10 -> 32.00; fee_weight_bonus 0.05 -> 33.50; repeat_fee_basis (method) -> 32.80. FACTOR CARD minimum (116.02; all-baseline 81.00): minimum_basis (method) core 68 -> 88.02; installment_component 49.51 -> 66.51; dispute_exclusion 6.44 -> 122.46; reversal_refigure 36.05 -> 152.07.
METHOD FACTORS, PAIRWISE TIER TABLE (one distinguishing input per pair): repeat_fee_basis (a) vs (b): late fees within 3 months (1 vs 2+); (a) vs (c) and (b) vs (c): fee level (repeat vs not). minimum_basis (a) vs (b)/(c): new balance below the floor; (b) vs (c): rounded percentage above the floor.
INDEPENDENCE: checked mechanically (transitive closure over compute names): no factor binding reads another factor's binding; shares and results are plain bindings.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: card_evt_fee_reversal one_reversal_per_fee (no reversal cites the fee); courtesy clause and full-amount clause overwritten with scoped tails; card_billing_dispute scope (the open dispute is on another charge); card_evt_payment_allocation scope (phone, 10:20 EDT, before the 17:00 ET cutoff); the allocation of the payment (lowest rate first, to the 8.99% plan) is the overnight back-office posting, which the desk does not hand-post (O-2/O-3), so no allocation row is in the gold. card_evt_statement minimum sentence (including the dispute exclusion clause) overwritten for the desk's re-figured minimum only.
SEED: ledger simulated day by day from base rules (statements, ADB interest 27.74%/365, late fees at the Reg Z safe-harbor levels capped at the minimum, minimum parts allocated lowest rate first to the 8.99% plan). current_balance 2707.15 = sum of balance deltas. Cross-product rows: tire set, road hazard 36-month certificate (17% x 168.99 = 28.73 per tire) and Lifetime Alignment Plan (249.99 - 40.00 tire bundle) on ticket T-30561847 = 1083.83, each exactly as its charter prices it; the promotional plan finances the pre-tax charter total, and the ticket's separate sales-tax line (kept outside charter computations by the tires charter) was paid at the counter.
PROBES (see worklog.md): decoy bank-card certificate, expired certificate, missing alignment plan, fee 13 months back, second 24-month plan, no cycle fee, dispute on the fee itself, dispute on a purchase from an earlier cycle, reversal of an earlier fee, missing dispute.
STANDARD SOLUTION: find_customers -> verify -> find_card_accounts -> find_card_transactions -> find_card_requests -> find_hazard_certificates -> find_alignment_plans -> find_tire_sets -> find_vehicles -> find_stores -> courtesy credit 35.00 on the 2026-09-19 fee -> hand-over, she pays 116.02 toward 2026-09-24.
DRAFT FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT: minimum rule -> the September-cycle fee must carry its courtesy credit; courtesy rule -> 0.80 share, 11.00 outright + 24.00 = 35.00; minimum 68 + 49.51 + 41.00 - 6.44 - 36.05 = 116.02. Agrees with gold.
user_scenario: You are Rosalind Achterberg-Nwosu, a physical therapist in Westerville, Ohio, calling Crestline's care line on a short break between patients. You carry a Crestline Auto Care Mastercard Preferred and you want to make this month's minimum payment on it right now, over the phone, so it is in well ahead of the due date — money has been tight since spring and you would rather not let it slide. You want the minimum payment for the statement that closed in September, the one due October 19, nothing more; you are not paying the full balance today. You are happy for the agent to look into your account and work out the figure, but the payment itself comes out of your checking account on file, so you will key it in yourself on the automated payment line once the agent sets it up for you. You speak briskly and a little apologetically, and you keep your answers short. When the agent asks to find your profile, you give your phone number as 6145550347. When the agent asks you to confirm your identity, you give your date of birth as 1984-07-29; if a further detail is needed you give your billing ZIP code 43081, and only if asked for your email you spell it as rosalind.achterberg.nwosu@lakeshoremail.com. If the agent asks for your card number you give only the last four digits, 3826. If the agent asks which statement or which due date, you say the one that closed on September 24 with the payment due October 19. You remember the September statement showing a minimum payment of 158.51; you mention it only if the agent asks what your statement says, or if the agent quotes you a minimum that differs from it — in that case you say it does not match what you saw printed and ask the agent to check it against your account, and once the agent explains why the figure is what it is, you accept the agent's figure without arguing. If the agent brings up the charge you disputed, you confirm you disputed a hardware store charge for an order that was never delivered, reported it to the bank at the start of October, and have not heard back. If the agent tells you something has been credited or adjusted on your account, you say that is a pleasant surprise and thank them, and you let the agent go ahead. If the agent offers autopay, paperless statements or any other extra, you politely say not today. When the agent hands the payment over to you with the account, the statement date and the amount to enter, you make the payment with exactly those details and then read back the confirmation number you are given. Once the payment has gone through and you have the confirmation number, you thank the agent and say goodbye.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: Value 116.02. minimum_basis: 3.0% x (2707.15 - 464.77) = 67.27 -> 68 > floor 40; installment_component: plan balance 464.77 > fixed payment 49.51 (1083.83 over 24 months at the Mastercard Preferred 8.99% rate, rounded up); past-due 0 (August minimum paid by 09-15 and 09-21); late fee of the cycle 41.00; dispute_exclusion: open dispute on the 214.60 outside purchase of 2026-09-08 -> 3.0% = 6.44 off; reversal_refigure: the 35.00 courtesy credit on the cycle fee -> 35.00 + 1.05 = 36.05 off; 68 + 49.51 + 0 + 41.00 - 6.44 - 36.05 = 116.02, nothing paid toward the statement since it closed.

edges.condition: Every card_late_fee row posted in the latest statement cycle that meets the courtesy credit conditions has a card_fee_reversal row with reversal_reason courtesy_waiver citing it in source_card_txn_id.
edges.policy_source: The minimum payment the desk takes on a statement is not fixed until every late fee posted in that statement's cycle that meets the courtesy credit conditions carries its courtesy credit.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The 41.00 late fee posted 2026-09-19 in the 2026-09-24 cycle meets the courtesy conditions (allowance 1, none used; the 108.51 August minimum was paid in full on 2026-09-21, before the 2026-09-24 statement closed) and no fee reversal cites it.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The courtesy call writes a 35.00 card_fee_reversal citing the fee; rev_off becomes 36.05 and the re-figured minimum falls from 152.07 to 116.02.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: One edge. The courtesy credit reads no payment toward the September statement, and the minimum reads the credit, so the only valid order is the credit then the payment.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the credit rev_off is 0 and the payment becomes 152.07 instead of 116.02; the card_fee_reversal row is missing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never names a late fee, a courtesy credit or any adjustment to ask for; it asks only for this month's minimum. The dispute line and the "credited or adjusted" line are reactions to what the agent says.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: pay_statement_minimum_b2a1a039 writes the payment with whatever amount it is given and checks no reversal; apply_courtesy_fee_credit_68b22b43 writes the reversal without checking any condition (task_tools.py: one ctx.find of the account for customer_id and one ctx.create).
